question:
A server engineer wants to control power usage on a Cisco UCS C-Series rack server down to the component level.
Which two components support specific power limits? (Choose two.)
theory: Cisco UCS Manager's power capping on C-Series rack servers can enforce specific limits on individual power-hungry components rather than only an overall server cap; the two components that support explicit, per-device power limits are the processor(s) and the memory (DIMMs), since these dominate a server's dynamic power draw and can be throttled via P-states/DVFS without disabling the server. Storage, network, and graphics controllers are managed as part of overall platform power budgeting but do not expose the same granular per-component limit settings. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Server Management/Power Control)
